claims.statement: EnginePreset is a Rust domain enum with exactly two values, qwen3 (the serde/Default value serialized as "qwen3") and whisperx, and it is the single decision input for diagnose, prepare, and transcription engine selection.

Fresh installs default to the Qwen3 preset: EnginePreset derives Default onto Qwen3, the settings store falls back to EnginePreset::default() when nothing is saved, and an application test verifies transcription with an untouched store uses Qwen3.
The engine preset persists in settings.json inside the app data root through LocalSettingsStore's load_engine_preset/save_engine_preset, exposed to the webview via the save_engine_preset IPC command.

worker_root switches on build profile: debug builds run the worker from the repo checkout (../worker next to the crate) while release builds run the staged copy under Tauri resources (resources/worker), and tauri.conf.json bundles both resources/worker and the external uv binary.

scripts/stage-sidecars.ts stages a pinned uv 0.12.5 aarch64-apple-darwin binary, verifying the SHA-256 of both the downloaded release archive and the extracted binary before installing it, and copies galpi_worker plus the requirements/lock files into src-tauri/resources/worker; uv_binary() resolves the binary from src-tauri/binaries/ in debug and beside the executable in release.

AppPaths::resolve derives the app data layout from Tauri's app_local_data_dir: per-engine venvs at engine/.venv and engine/qwen3/.venv, per-engine bin dirs holding a linked ffmpeg, model manifests under models/ (ready.json, qwen3-ready.json), and cache/ (huggingface, torch, uv) plus python/ for uv-managed interpreters, so removing the app data folder reclaims the multi-gigabyte caches.

The Qwen3 stack lives in its own virtualenv (engine/qwen3/.venv) so the pinned WhisperX environment never shares dependency versions with the candidate stack; the transcription adapter selects the interpreter per preset, and preparing or reinstalling one venv cannot disturb the other's pins.

src-tauri/build.rs compiles FNV-1a fingerprints of worker/requirements.txt and worker/requirements-qwen3.txt into the binary as GALPI_WHISPERX_REQUIREMENTS_HASH and GALPI_QWEN3_REQUIREMENTS_HASH, emits rerun-if-changed for both files, and fails the build if a requirements file is missing rather than fingerprinting nothing.

Engine readiness markers encode "<version>+<requirements-hash>" — whisperx_marker() is ENGINE_VERSION (3.8.6) plus the WhisperX requirements hash, qwen3_marker() is QWEN3_ENGINE_VERSION (2) plus the Qwen3 hash — so editing a pinned dependency alone invalidates every existing virtualenv: the next build compiles a new hash, the marker comparison fails, the engine reports not ready, and prepare reinstalls the venv and rewrites the marker without any manual version bump.

The version half of the markers is coupled across files and must move together: the WhisperX marker filename ready-3.8.6 is hardcoded in paths.rs and the manifest check compares against ENGINE_VERSION (matching the worker's version("whisperx") only while the pin stays at 3.8.6), while the Qwen3 marker filename ready-qwen3-2 comes from QWEN3_ENGINE_VERSION and the worker's manifest payload hardcodes "qwen3": "2".

status() computes readiness per preset: engine_ready requires the preset's .venv/bin/python plus a marker file exactly equal to the current version+hash marker; models_ready requires a JSON manifest with protocol==1 and the engine's version field, the preset's Hugging Face hub directories (WhisperX: large-v3-turbo, wav2vec2-large-xlsr-korean, pyannote community-1; Qwen3: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B, Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B, the same pyannote model) plus the converted MLX weights file for Qwen3; ffmpeg_ready requires the preset's engine bin ffmpeg file.

EnvironmentStatus carries the requested preset's engine/models/ffmpeg booleans, both presets' summary booleans (qwen3Ready, whisperxReady) so the UI can badge both engines, dataDirectory (the app data root), defaultOutputDirectory ($HOME/Documents/Galpi, /tmp fallback), and a display engineVersion string; is_ready() is the conjunction of the three per-preset booleans.

Transcription is gated on readiness: run_transcription loads the saved preset, re-diagnoses, and fails with SETUP_REQUIRED when the selected preset is not ready, so worker transcription only ever runs after the gate passes.

setup.rs::prepare resolves AppPaths, creates directories, builds install and model environments, and short-circuits with a ready phase when status(preset).is_ready(); otherwise it installs the engine if the marker check fails, runs the worker prepare subprocess if models or ffmpeg are missing, and finally recomputes status, failing with SETUP_INCOMPLETE unless is_ready() — marker files and manifests, not worker exit codes, are the source of truth.

Engine install runs three uv invocations under process_environment: uv python install 3.12 into the app-managed UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR, uv venv --clear (so a failed first attempt leaves retries idempotent instead of tripping uv's refusal), and uv pip install from the preset's lock file — WhisperX from requirements.lock with --require-hashes, Qwen3 from requirements-qwen3.lock — writing the readiness marker only after pip succeeds.

The worker prepare subprocess is spawned as <preset python> -m galpi_worker prepare --manifest <models manifest> --engine-bin <bin dir> --engine <preset>, and the worker CLI's argparse default for --engine is whisperx while the host always passes --engine explicitly, so the saved preset — never the CLI default — decides the engine.

model_cache.rs imports the three known model directories from ~/.cache/huggingface/hub into the app cache (hard links with a copy fallback, symlinks recreated only when their canonical target stays inside the source repo, escaping links rejected); the import is best-effort — a failure is logged as an event and treated as zero imported.

can_use_offline_cache is true only when all three model directories imported and no non-blank Hugging Face token is configured; when true, the model environment gains HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, and Qwen3 transcription always forces both flags because it runs strictly after the readiness gate and must load exclusively from the prepared cache.

process_environment builds the spawned worker's environment deterministically rather than inheriting the shell's: HOME (with /tmp fallback), ko_KR.UTF-8 locale, PYTHONUTF8/PYTHONSAFEPATH/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, PYTHONPATH at the worker root, HF_HOME/TORCH_HOME/UV_CACHE_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR inside app data, telemetry and implicit-token opt-outs (HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY, HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN, PYANNOTE_METRICS_ENABLED=false, DO_NOT_TRACK), PATH prepending the WhisperX engine bin dir (engine/bin, where prepare links ffmpeg — the entry does not switch with the preset), preserved TMPDIR, and an optional trimmed HF_TOKEN; assistant_environment extends it with GALPI_ASSISTANT_API_KEY and optional base URL and reasoning-effort overrides.

The worker's prepare step links ffmpeg into the engine bin dir — a symlink to the imageio-ffmpeg binary with a copy+chmod 0o755 fallback — which is exactly the file ffmpeg_ready inspects and what transcription uses to decode audio.

The worker's prepare pipelines diverge per engine: WhisperX loads large-v3-turbo on CPU int8 plus the Korean aligner and pyannote diarizer on MPS-with-one-CPU-retry, freeing each model before the next, and writes models/ready.json; Qwen3 downloads the ASR and aligner snapshots concurrently (two workers, tqdm bars summed by DownloadReporter into one GB figure throttled to one event per second), converts the ASR snapshot to 8-bit MLX weights via a .partial staging directory atomically moved into cache/mlx/qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit, downloads and warms the gated pyannote model with the settings token, and writes models/qwen3-ready.json.

Qwen3 preparation ends by actually running the engine: verify_qwen3_session loads the converted weights and transcribes one second of silence, failing with a directory-naming RuntimeError when weights.safetensors is missing, so a bad conversion or missing runtime dependency surfaces during prepare instead of during a real meeting.

The webview reflects the environment through EnvironmentStatus parsed with Zod at the Tauri boundary: TauriBackend.diagnose invokes diagnose_environment and parses through environmentSchema (enginePreset as z.enum(["qwen3","whisperx"]), all booleans and strings), the flat camelCase shape mirroring the host struct one-to-one, and toJobEvent renames the worker protocol's engine_version onto the domain field engineVersion for prepared events.

Switching presets saves then re-diagnoses so the setup panel stays truthful: the controller's switchEngine calls saveEnginePreset and immediately diagnoses (no Apply step), start() diagnoses at launch, and prepare() renders the completed job's status; a controller test pins that switching persists the preset and re-renders the panel from the new diagnosis.

AppView.setEnvironment syncs the engine-preset radios, badges both engines from qwen3Ready/whisperxReady (기본 / 이전 엔진), renders the engine/models/ffmpeg status rows and engineVersion, and toggles the setup panel between 준비 완료 and 설정 필요 (relabeling the prepare button accordingly), gating the panel and stage rail on readiness — with DOM tests covering both states.

Focused tests pin this subsystem's contracts: engine.rs (default wire value, unknown preset rejection), application tests (Qwen3 default followed by saved-preset switching; prepare follows the selected preset), setup.rs tests (Qwen3 model ids keep the Qwen/ repo-id shape cache_dir_name relies on), model_cache tests (hard-link import with safe symlinks; offline mode requires the complete tokenless cache), and the settings store test (engine preset persists while secrets stay out of settings.json).

The uv engine installs run with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed, so only interpreters uv itself installed into the app-managed UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR are candidates; a system Python 3.12 that happens to be on PATH is never selected.

The PATH entry in process_environment always prepends the WhisperX engine bin (engine/bin) regardless of the selected preset, so WhisperX transcription resolves the linked ffmpeg from PATH, while the Qwen3 stack does not depend on that entry and invokes the imageio-ffmpeg binary directly through ffmpeg_executable().
